name: Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch
blurb: Ibex, marmots and eagles around the longest glacier in the Alps.

tip.title: Thin out the marmots
tip.text: Marmots are a staple of golden eagles, foxes and stoats. Set Alpine marmot to -100% and watch those predators and the hares they turn to.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Short alpine summers and intense light at altitude set how long plants can grow on the high slopes.
Break down dead plants, animals and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
The dominant subalpine conifer on the south side of the site. Its shoots and needles are winter food for chamois and ibex.

nodes.name: Alpine meadow plants
nodes.desc: Grasses and herbs of the alpine meadows above the treeline, the main summer food of marmots, chamois and ibex.

nodes.name: Spotted nutcracker
nodes.desc: Eats Swiss stone pine seeds and spreads them, since the heavy seeds are barely wind-dispersed.
Picks insects from alpine pasture in summer and fruit in winter. Flocks gather around huts and ski areas for scraps.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: The largest herbivore of the valleys and forest edges, grazing grasses and browsing shrubs and shoots.
Grazes alpine meadows in summer and moves into forest in winter, eating conifer needles and bark. Lynx and wolves are its natural predators.
A small hunter of the mountains that takes voles, hares and young marmots.
Widespread hunter and scavenger from valley to alpine meadows, taking hares, marmots, birds and carrion.
Scavenges carcasses and also takes the nestlings of other birds such as choughs.
Top aerial predator of the high Alps. Marmots and hares are staple prey, it may take young ibex, and in winter it feeds on carrion.
Reintroduced to Switzerland. Hunts chamois, roe and red deer and hares, mainly in forest and rocky ground.
Has returned to the Alps in recent decades. Takes deer and chamois, and the Alpine ibex lives on steep ground that gives it some protection.

story: Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch is located in south-western Switzerland between the cantons of Bern and Valais. The protected site covers an area of 82,388 ha and contains the largest glaciated area in western Eurasia, including the Aletsch Glacier. It is home to animals such as the chamois, alpine ibex, and red deer.
matters: The area is the first World Natural Heritage site in the Alps and comprises the largest continuous area of ice in the Alps. It shelters numerous plant and vertebrate species adapted to high altitudes and extreme weather.
